paper_metadata.title: Effects of Isothermal Solution Treatment on Microstructure Evolution and Tensile Properties of High Strength Near-β Ti Alloy
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: The influence of slow cooling rate and the isothermal holding temperature in isothermal solution treatment on microstructure evolution and tensile properties of near-β Ti alloy was investigated in this work.

The raw material Ti-5321 alloy was provided by Northwest Institute for Non-ferrous Metal Research, China (Ref 22). It was hot rolled in α + β phase field into Φ 20 mm in diameter.
It was hot rolled in α + β phase field into Φ 20 mm in diameter.
Firstly, the samples were solutionized at 900 °C for 0.5 h, and then these samples were slowly cooled to various targeted temperatures

these samples were slowly cooled to various targeted temperatures (i.e., 650, 700, 750, 800 and 830 °C) ... The slow cooling rates from 900 °C to targeted holding temperatures were selected as 2 and 10 °C/min.
isothermally holding for 1 h followed by water quenching
Lastly, aging treatment was conducted at 600 °C for 8 h. During aging treatment the samples with thickness of 5 mm were heated to 600 °C at 10 °C/min.
The sample slowly cooled to 800 °C obtained hardness similar to that of β solution treated alloy (300 ± 5 HV).

In the samples slowly cooled to 830 and 800 °C, the diffraction peaks from α phase were very weak but still could be identified, hence it was thought that α phase has been formed when the samples were slowly cooled to 830 and 800 °C.
plenty of colonies consisting of parallel α needles were formed within β grains after holding at 830 and 800 °C for 1 h.
After aging treatment, secondary α precipitates having short-rod shape and nanoscale size were formed besides α colonies.
The a plates showed comparable larger thickness, length and aspect ratio ( > 30) but had lower number density.
the fine a particles exhibited short-rod shape, as well as smaller thickness, length and aspect ratio (< 5).
the phase transformation from b to a obeys the BOR relationships {110}b//{0001}a and [111]b//[11–-20]a
When held below 750 °C, basketweave microstructures could be obtained after aging treatment, because most of α phase had been formed upon solution stage with plate-like shape.
the sample with basketweave microstructure showed plenty of a plates and some a particles in nearby regions
equiaxed β grains were visible shown in Fig. 3(a) and (b). The average diameter of β grains was measured to be 180 ± 20 μm
During the final aging treatment, α lamellas with same orientation originated from β grain boundaries and grew into grains, forming Widmanstatten structure.
some precipitation free zone (PFZ) was formed and developed into β blocks neighboring primary α plates.
the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation and area reduction were 1470, 1497 MPa, 4 and 5.8%, respectively.
the yield strength was decreased from 1470 ± 17 to 1179 ± 20 MPa with the holding temperature decreasing from 800 to 750 °C

the elongation increased from 4.0 ± 1 to 16.7 ± 0.6%.
It was thought that α phase would be formed upon three stages above, leading to precipitation hardening.

During heat treatment α stabilizers would be concentrated in α phase, and β stabilizers, i.e., Mo, V and Cr, would be excluded and enriched in β matrix. Such partitioning of solute atoms could strengthen β matrix and weaken the driving force of α precipitation.
This suggested that the alloy with basketweave microstructure was deformed by dislocation shearing mechanism.
These secondary a precipitates were more efﬁcient to strengthen alloy, be- cause they could produce higher density of a/b inter- faces impeding dislocation slipping.

conflicts.description: Yield strength of sample with 10 °C/min cooling and 800 °C isothermal holding after aging is reported as 1470 MPa in abstract and 1470 ± 17 MPa in text; ultimate tensile strength is 1497 MPa in abstract vs 1494 ± 7 MPa for 2 °C/min in text.

evidence.quote: the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation and area reduction were 1470, 1497 MPa, 4 and 5.8%, respectively.

For the slow cooling rate of 2 °C/min and isothermal holding temperature of 800 °C, the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation and area reduction of the sample after aging treatment reached to 1458 ± 15, 1494 ± 7 MPa, 4.4 ± 0.5 and 4.6 ± 1%, respectively.
